newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: N.Korea defector shot near Seoul, in serious state.
newsitem.headline: N.Korea defector shot near Seoul, in serious state.

text.p: Two gunmen have shot and seriously wounded a North Korean defector near Seoul in an attack suspected to have been ordered by Pyongyang, police officers said on Sunday.
"We don"t have any proof at the moment but we suspect North Korea ordered the men to carry out the attack to warn the South after Hwang Jang-yop's defection," one senior officer told Reuters.
Tensions on the divided Korean peninsula have flared since Wednesday, when Hwang, a senior adviser to North Korean leader Kim Jong-il, arrived by taxi at Seoul"s Beijing mission.

South Korea says Hwang is seeking asylum in the South, while a furious North Korea insists he was kidnapped. Hwang, ranked 24th in the Stalinist state"s hierarchy, would be the most senior Pyongyang official to seek asylum in the South.
The senior officer, who asked not to be named, identified the injured man as Li Il-nam (known in South Korea as Lee Han-yong), and described him as the nephew of a girlfriend of the Pyongyang leader.

Li, 36, was shot in the head and chest outside his temporary home at Bundang, just south of Seoul, late on Saturday, the police officer said. A nurse at a nearby hospital said the defector later underwent surgery but he remained unconscious.
Another police officer said a neighbour had found Li lying outside his apartment and reported the incident to police.
Police believed the attackers used silencers as neighbours heard no gunshots, he said. An analysis of two used cartridges at the scene showed the weapons used were Belgian-made handguns.
The attack took place as China agonised over what to do with Hwang, a top Pyongyang ideologue who is a member of the powerful secretariat of the North's ruling Workers' (Communist) Party.

Allowing Hwang to go to Seoul, where he could be expected to reveal crucial secrets about the North Korean state, would offend Beijing's old communist comrades, while sending him back to Pyongyang would endanger China's ties with its new capitalist friend which has already proved a valuable investor.
Hwang"s apparent betrayal has caused a massive loss of face for a North Korean government already reeling from severe food shortages and economic disasters.
Fearing retaliation, Seoul has ordered tighter security at all its overseas missions.
Police in Seoul and the surrounding Kyonggi Province have been placed on alert since the attack on Li and a search is under way for the gunmen.

Li, who came to South Korea in the early 1980s from Europe where he had been studying, is the first North Korean defector to be shot in the South since the end of the 1950-53 Korean War, according to police.
China, one of North Korea's few remaining allies since the collapse of the Soviet Union, fought on Pyongyang"s side in the war.
Despite the 1953 truce, the two Koreas have remained implacable foes and their tense common border, bristling with advanced weapons, is today the last Cold War frontier.
